title: One of several types
description:
A `std::variant<int, double, std::string>` holds exactly one of those three at a time, and knows which.

Write `std::string describe(const Value& value)`:

| Holds | Returns |
|---|---|
| an `int` | `"int 5"` |
| a `double` | `"double 2.500000"` (`std::to_string`) |
| a `std::string` | `"text hello"` |

Use `std::visit` with the `Overloaded` helper provided: you give it one lambda per alternative, and the compiler refuses to build if you forget one.
unitTests:
TEST("each alternative") { CHECK_EQ(describe(Value{ 5 }), "int 5"); CHECK_EQ(describe(Value{ 2.5 }), "double 2.500000"); CHECK_EQ(describe(Value{ std::string{ "hello" } }), "text hello"); }
TEST("a variant can change what it holds") { Value v{ 1 }; v = std::string{ "now text" }; CHECK_EQ(describe(v), "text now text"); v = 0.5; CHECK_EQ(describe(v), "double 0.500000"); }
